export const meta = {
  name: 'py2node-bucketize-migration',
  description: 'Port /workspace/dataset/test5.py to ESM Node in /output, then differential-test to byte parity vs the reference binary',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Implement' },
    { title: 'Differential' },
    { title: 'Fix' },
    { title: 'Audit' },
  ],
}

const REF = '/workspace/dataset/test5_executable'
const OUT = '/output'

const SPEC = [
  '# Migration target',
  '',
  'Source Python (/workspace/dataset/test5.py):',
  '',
  '    import argparse',
  '    from boltons.iterutils import bucketize',
  '',
  '    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()',
  "    parser.add_argument('--a', type=str, required=True, help='Comma-separated numbers')",
  '    args = parser.parse_args()',
  '',
  "    numbers = [int(x) for x in args.a.split(',')]",
  '    result = bucketize(numbers, lambda x: x % 2 == 0)',
  '    print(result)',
  '',
  'Reference binary (the ground truth, run it freely): ' + REF,
  'Never run `python`. Only run the reference binary and `node`.',
  '',
  '# HARD REQUIREMENTS (violating any invalidates the work)',
  '',
  '1. Pure JavaScript for Node.js. ES Modules ONLY: `import` / `export`.',
  '   `require()` and `module.exports` are STRICTLY PROHIBITED anywhere.',
  '2. Every generated file MUST use the `.mjs` extension.',
  '3. ZERO external dependencies. No npm packages. `import` may ONLY reference',
  '   local relative paths (with full `.mjs` suffix) or `node:` builtins.',
  '   Do NOT create package.json, node_modules, or any lockfile.',
  '4. No embedding/among/spawning of Python. No child_process to any python.',
  '5. All files under ' + OUT + '. Entry file MUST be exactly ' + OUT + '/test5.mjs',
  '6. Hierarchical: split the library into multiple focused modules under',
  '   ' + OUT + '/lib/**, each exposing its interface via `export`.',
  '   Suggested (adapt as sensible):',
  '     lib/runtime/stdio.mjs        write to stdout/stderr, exit-code handling',
  '     lib/python/unicode.mjs       Unicode Nd digit values, White_Space, printability',
  '     lib/python/repr.mjs          Python repr()/str() for str/bool/int/list/dict',
  '     lib/python/int.mjs           Python int(str) semantics -> BigInt',
  '     lib/python/exceptions.mjs    ValueError + CPython traceback rendering',
  '     lib/cli/argparse.mjs         the argparse subset actually used',
  '     lib/cli/parser.mjs           this program\'s concrete parser definition',
  '     lib/boltons/iterutils.mjs    bucketize',
  '7. Do not reference, name, or import any third-party JS library.',
  '8. Use `process.exitCode = N` and let the event loop drain, rather than',
  '   `process.exit(N)`, so large stdout writes are never truncated on a pipe.',
  '',
  '# VERIFIED BEHAVIOURAL SPEC (already measured byte-exactly from the reference)',
  '',
  '## A. Success output (stdout, exit 0)',
  '',
  'Python `print(dict)` of the bucketize result, then a single "\\n".',
  'dict repr: "{" + entries joined by ", " + "}"; each entry "KEY: VALUE".',
  'Keys are Python bools -> "True" / "False". Values are lists ->',
  '"[" + items joined by ", " + "]". Empty dict -> "{}", empty list -> "[]".',
  'Integers render as plain decimal, arbitrary precision, no "n" suffix,',
  'no separators. Negative zero normalises to "0".',
  '',
  'Measured examples (stdout, exit 0):',
  '  --a 1,2,3,4,5,6   -> {False: [1, 3, 5], True: [2, 4, 6]}',
  '  --a 2,4,6         -> {True: [2, 4, 6]}',
  '  --a 1,3,5         -> {False: [1, 3, 5]}',
  '  --a 2,1           -> {True: [2], False: [1]}',
  '  --a 4,2,3,1,6,5   -> {True: [4, 2, 6], False: [3, 1, 5]}',
  '  --a -3            -> {False: [-3]}',
  '  --a -4            -> {True: [-4]}',
  '  --a "+5,-6"       -> {False: [5], True: [-6]}',
  '  --a "0,-0,00"     -> {True: [0, 0, 0]}',
  '  --a 007,08        -> {False: [7], True: [8]}',
  '  --a "1_0,2"       -> {True: [10, 2]}',
  '  --a " 1 , 2 "     -> {False: [1], True: [2]}',
  '  --a 9007199254740993 -> {False: [9007199254740993]}',
  '  --a 123456789012345678901234567890 -> {True: [123456789012345678901234567890]}',
  '  --a 123456789012345678901234567891 -> {False: [123456789012345678901234567891]}',
  '  --a -123456789012345678901234567891 -> {False: [-123456789012345678901234567891]}',
  '',
  '## B. bucketize (boltons.iterutils)',
  '',
  'bucketize(src, keyfunc) returns a dict: for each item in order, append it to',
  'the list at keyfunc(item). KEY ORDER IS FIRST-INSERTION ORDER, not sorted.',
  'So you MUST use an insertion-ordered container keyed by the boolean',
  '(a Map with boolean keys is ideal). Implement it generically and honestly',
  '(iterate the source once, in order).',
  '',
  '## C. Parity of the arithmetic',
  '',
  'The key is `x % 2 == 0`. Values are arbitrary-precision, so use BigInt.',
  'CAUTION: Python and JS agree here only because the test is `== 0`.',
  'Python -3 % 2 == 1 (never 0); JS -3n % 2n === -1n (never 0n). Both give',
  'false for odd and true for even, so `x % 2n === 0n` is correct. Note it',
  'in a comment so nobody "fixes" it into a bug.',
  '',
  '## D. Python int(str) semantics -> BigInt',
  '',
  'Grammar (base 10):',
  '  WS* [ + | - ]? DIGITS ( "_" DIGITS )* WS*',
  'where DIGITS is one or more Unicode General_Category=Nd characters.',
  '',
  'Rules verified against the reference:',
  '  * Leading/trailing whitespace is stripped. The whitespace set is exactly',
  '    the Unicode White_Space property. Verified accepted: U+0009 U+000A',
  '    U+000B U+000C U+000D U+0020 U+0085 U+00A0 U+1680 U+2000..U+200A',
  '    U+2028 U+2029 U+202F U+205F U+3000. Verified REJECTED (NOT whitespace',
  '    for int()): U+001C U+001D U+001E U+001F and U+200B.',
  '    In Node, `/\\p{White_Space}/u` matches exactly the accepted set and',
  '    rejects U+001C..U+001F and U+200B -- confirmed. Use that, do not',
  '    hand-roll a list, and do NOT use JS String.prototype.trim() (its set',
  '    differs: it includes U+FEFF and excludes U+0085).',
  '  * No whitespace is permitted between the sign and the digits, or inside',
  '    the digits. "- 3" invalid, "+ 3" invalid, "3 4" invalid, "1 000" invalid.',
  '  * Any Unicode Nd digit is accepted and contributes its decimal value.',
  '    Verified: "\\u0663,\\u0664" -> {False: [3], True: [4]};',
  '    fullwidth "\\uFF11,\\uFF12" -> {False: [1], True: [2]};',
  '    Myanmar "\\u1045" -> {False: [5]};',
  '    a 23-char fullwidth numeral -> {False: [12345678901234567890123]}.',
  '    Digit scripts may be MIXED within one literal (the reference accepts',
  '    per-character decimal values; verify this yourself).',
  '    To get a value from an Nd code point: Unicode Nd runs are contiguous',
  '    aligned decades, so walk back at most 9 code points while the previous',
  '    code point is still Nd to find the run start, then value = cp - start.',
  '    Verified correct for U+0030, U+0039, U+0663, U+1045, U+FF19, U+1D7CE,',
  '    U+1E959. Do not use parseInt on non-ASCII digits (it returns NaN).',
  '  * NON-Nd numerics are REJECTED: "\\u00B2" (superscript two), "\\u00BD"',
  '    (one half), "\\u2165" (Roman numeral VI) all raise.',
  '  * Underscores: single, strictly between digits. "1_0" ok. Invalid:',
  '    "1__0", "_1", "1_", and (verify) "+_1", "-_1".',
  '  * Rejected forms verified: "" (empty), " " (whitespace only), "1.5",',
  '    "-3.5", "abc", "0x10", "0b11", "1\\u200B".',
  '',
  '## E. int() digit limit (CPython sys.int_max_str_digits = 4300)',
  '',
  'If the literal is syntactically VALID and its digit count exceeds 4300,',
  'int() raises a DIFFERENT ValueError:',
  '  Exceeds the limit (4300 digits) for integer string conversion: value has',
  '  N digits; use sys.set_int_max_str_digits() to increase the limit',
  '(one single line; N is the digit count).',
  '',
  'Digit-count semantics, all verified:',
  '  * Counts digit characters, INCLUDING leading zeros. 4400 "0" chars ->',
  '    "value has 4400 digits" (even though the value is 0).',
  '  * 4000 zeros + 400 nines -> "value has 4400 digits".',
  '  * Underscores are NOT counted: 2200 repetitions of "9_" plus "9"',
  '    (2201 digits, 2200 underscores) parses FINE.',
  '  * The sign is NOT counted: "-" + 4301 nines -> "value has 4301 digits".',
  '  * Surrounding whitespace is irrelevant: " " + 4301 nines + " " ->',
  '    "value has 4301 digits".',
  '  * 4300 digits is ACCEPTED; 4301 raises.',
  '',
  'PRECEDENCE (verified): syntactic validity is checked FIRST. A string that is',
  'both invalid AND long yields the "invalid literal" error, not the limit one:',
  '  5000 "a" chars                  -> invalid literal (with the full 5000-char repr)',
  '  4301 nines + "a"                -> invalid literal',
  '  4301 nines + "_"                -> invalid literal',
  '  100 nines + "a" + 4300 nines    -> invalid literal',
  '',
  '## F. The "invalid literal" ValueError message',
  '',
  '  invalid literal for int() with base 10: <REPR>',
  '',
  '<REPR> is Python repr() of the ORIGINAL, UNSTRIPPED segment string.',
  'You must implement Python 3 str repr() faithfully:',
  '  * Quote choice: use "\'" normally; if the string contains "\'" and does',
  '    NOT contain \'"\', use \'"\' as the delimiter instead.',
  '    Verified: a\'b -> "a\'b" (double quotes)',
  '              a"b -> \'a"b\' (single quotes)',
  '              a\'b"c -> \'a\\\'b"c\' (single quotes, backslash-escaped apostrophe)',
  '  * Always escape a literal backslash as two backslashes. Verified: a\\b -> \'a\\\\b\'',
  '  * Escape the delimiter with a backslash. Never escape the other quote.',
  '  * Short escapes: TAB -> \\t, LF -> \\n, CR -> \\r. Verified: a<TAB>b -> \'a\\tb\',',
  '    a<LF>b -> \'a\\nb\'.',
  '  * Every other NON-PRINTABLE character is escaped by code point:',
  '      cp < 0x100     -> \\xHH   (2 lower-case hex digits)',
  '      cp < 0x10000   -> \\uHHHH (4 lower-case hex digits)',
  '      otherwise      -> \\UHHHHHHHH (8 lower-case hex digits)',
  '    Verified: U+0007 -> \'\\x07\'; "\\u001C1" -> \'\\x1c1\'; "1\\u200B" ->',
  '    \'1\\u200b\'; "a\\u00E9\\u200B" -> \'a\\u00e9\\u200b\' i.e. printable',
  '    non-ASCII is emitted RAW while U+200B is escaped.',
  '  * PRINTABILITY = Python str.isprintable(): a character is NON-printable',
  '    iff its General_Category is one of Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp, Zs,',
  '    EXCEPT that U+0020 (plain space) IS printable.',
  '    In Node this is exactly /[\\p{Cc}\\p{Cf}\\p{Cs}\\p{Co}\\p{Cn}\\p{Zl}\\p{Zp}\\p{Zs}]/u',
  '    -- all ten property escapes are supported and were confirmed to give',
  '    the right answers for U+0020, U+0007, U+001C, U+00A0, U+200B, U+00E9,',
  '    U+1F389, U+0378, U+2028, U+3000.',
  '    NOTE U+00A0 and U+3000 are Zs => NON-printable => escaped in repr,',
  '    even though int() strips them as whitespace. Both facts coexist.',
  '  * Iterate by CODE POINT, not UTF-16 unit, so astral chars work.',
  '    Verified: emoji U+1F389 is printable and emitted raw.',
  '',
  '## G. Traceback for the ValueError (stderr, exit code 1)',
  '',
  'Byte-exact, from od -c of the reference. Line by line:',
  '  Traceback (most recent call last):',
  '  <2 spaces>File "test5.py", line 8, in <module>',
  '  <4 spaces>numbers = [int(x) for x in args.a.split(\',\')]',
  '  <15 spaces>^^^^^^',
  '  ValueError: <message>',
  '  [PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script \'test5\' due to unhandled exception!',
  'and a trailing newline after the last line.',
  'The caret line is exactly 15 spaces then exactly 6 "^" (it underlines',
  '"int(x)", which starts at column 11 of the 4-space-indented source line).',
  'The final [PYI-...] line is the PyInstaller bootloader\'s; <pid> is the',
  'process id and varies per run, so emit `process.pid` there and add a',
  'comment saying so. Exit code is 1.',
  'Only the FIRST failing segment raises (the comprehension stops there).',
  '',
  '## H. argparse emulation',
  '',
  'prog name: the reference reports `test5_executable` (argparse uses',
  'basename(sys.argv[0])). Since the reference binary IS the program being',
  'ported, hardcode the prog string as `test5_executable` in ONE named',
  'constant so stderr/usage match the reference byte-for-byte, and comment',
  'why. Do not derive it from process.argv[1].',
  '',
  'usage line (used by both --help and errors):',
  '  usage: test5_executable [-h] --a A',
  '',
  '--help / -h -> STDOUT, exit 0, exactly these bytes (129 bytes total,',
  'verified by od; help column starts at column 14):',
  '  usage: test5_executable [-h] --a A',
  '  <blank line>',
  '  options:',
  '  <2 spaces>-h, --help<2 spaces>show this help message and exit',
  '  <2 spaces>--a A<7 spaces>Comma-separated numbers',
  'with a trailing newline. Verify with `diff <(ref --help) <(node test5.mjs --help)`.',
  'Nothing goes to stderr for --help.',
  '',
  'Errors -> STDERR, exit code 2, two lines:',
  '  usage: test5_executable [-h] --a A',
  '  test5_executable: error: <detail>',
  'Verified details:',
  '  no args              -> the following arguments are required: --a',
  '  --a (no value)       -> argument --a: expected one argument',
  '  --a -abc             -> argument --a: expected one argument',
  '  --a -3,-4,0          -> argument --a: expected one argument',
  '  --b 1                -> the following arguments are required: --a',
  '  -a 1,2               -> the following arguments are required: --a',
  '  --                   -> the following arguments are required: --a',
  '  --a 1 extra          -> unrecognized arguments: extra',
  '',
  'PRECEDENCE (verified): "expected one argument" is raised during parsing;',
  'the required-argument check runs NEXT; the unrecognized-arguments check',
  'runs LAST. That is why `--b 1` and `-a 1,2` report the missing --a rather',
  'than the unknown option. Reproduce this ordering.',
  '',
  'Other verified behaviours:',
  '  * `--a=1,2` inline value form works.',
  '  * repeated `--a 1 --a 2` -> last one wins -> {True: [2]}.',
  '  * A value starting with "-" is accepted when it looks like a negative',
  '    number. argparse\'s test is /^-\\d+$|^-\\d*\\.\\d+$/ (ASCII digits only)',
  '    and applies because this parser has no negative-number-like options.',
  '    Verified: `--a -3` -> {False: [-3]}; `--a -4` -> {True: [-4]};',
  '    `--a -3.5` -> ValueError on \'-3.5\' (so it WAS consumed as a value).',
  '  * Follow real argparse _parse_optional order so these all fall out:',
  '    empty string -> value; first char not "-" -> value; exact option-string',
  '    match -> option; single "-" -> value; "=" form; abbreviation match;',
  '    negative-number match -> value; contains a space -> value; else unknown',
  '    optional. YOU MUST verify these against the reference yourself:',
  '    `--a -`, `--a "-3 -4"`, `--h`, `--he`, `--ab`, `--a 1 --`, `--a -- -3`.',
  '  * Long-option abbreviation is real argparse behaviour: `--h`/`--he`',
  '    uniquely prefix `--help`. Check what the reference actually does and',
  '    match it.',
  '',
  '# Method',
  '',
  'Treat the reference binary as an oracle. For every claim above and every',
  'edge you touch, run the reference and your Node version and diff the',
  'stdout, the stderr, and the exit code. Use `diff` on captured files rather',
  'than eyeballing. Remember the [PYI-...] pid differs between runs -- that',
  'single number is the ONLY permitted stderr difference.',
].join('\n')

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const FINDINGS_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['mismatches', 'notes'],
  properties: {
    notes: { type: 'string', description: 'What you tested and the overall verdict' },
    mismatches: {
      type: 'array',
      description: 'Confirmed divergences from the reference, or violated hard requirements. Empty if none.',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        additionalProperties: false,
        required: ['title', 'repro', 'expected', 'actual', 'severity'],
        properties: {
          title: { type: 'string' },
          repro: { type: 'string', description: 'Exact shell command(s) that demonstrate it' },
          expected: { type: 'string', description: 'Reference stdout/stderr/exit' },
          actual: { type: 'string', description: 'Node stdout/stderr/exit' },
          file: { type: 'string', description: 'Implicated file if known' },
          severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocker', 'major', 'minor'] },
        },
      },
    },
  },
}

const VERDICT_SCHEMA = {
  type: 'object',
  additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['real', 'reason'],
  properties: {
    real: { type: 'boolean', description: 'true if the divergence genuinely reproduces right now' },
    reason: { type: 'string' },
  },
}

const DIMENSIONS = [
  {
    key: 'int-grammar',
    prompt: [
      'Differential-test Python int(str) GRAMMAR parity: signs, underscores,',
      'whitespace stripping (the full Unicode White_Space set AND the',
      'non-whitespace lookalikes U+001C..U+001F, U+200B, U+FEFF), empty and',
      'whitespace-only segments, floats, hex/binary/octal prefixes, letters,',
      'internal spaces, "--3", "+_1", "-_1", "1_0", "1__0", "_1", "1_".',
      'Also comma splitting: trailing/leading/double commas, a lone ",".',
      'Confirm only the FIRST bad segment raises.',
    ].join(' '),
  },
  {
    key: 'unicode-digits',
    prompt: [
      'Differential-test Unicode Nd digit handling: Arabic-Indic, extended',
      'Arabic-Indic, Devanagari, Bengali, Myanmar, Thai, fullwidth, and astral',
      'digit blocks (U+1D7CE.., U+1E950..). Test MIXED scripts inside one',
      'literal, digits combined with signs and underscores, and long',
      'multi-script numbers. Also confirm non-Nd numerics are rejected:',
      'U+00B2 U+00B9 U+00BD U+2153 U+2165 U+3007 U+1369 (check each against',
      'the reference; report only real divergences). Verify the Nd decimal',
      'value derivation is right across many blocks by comparing printed output.',
    ].join(' '),
  },
  {
    key: 'bigint-limit',
    prompt: [
      'Differential-test arbitrary precision and the 4300-digit limit.',
      'Exercise: values far beyond 2**53 and beyond 2**64, negative huge',
      'values, parity of huge odd/even values, exactly 4299/4300/4301/5000',
      'digits, leading zeros inflating the count (4400 zeros), underscores not',
      'counted, sign not counted, whitespace not counted, and the precedence',
      'rule that an invalid-AND-long literal yields the invalid-literal error.',
      'Also verify huge output is not truncated when stdout is a pipe or is',
      'redirected to a file (this is why process.exit must not be used):',
      'compare byte counts with `wc -c` and `cmp`.',
    ].join(' '),
  },
  {
    key: 'repr-escaping',
    prompt: [
      'Differential-test the Python repr() used in the ValueError message.',
      'Cover: quote selection (apostrophe only, double-quote only, both),',
      'backslashes, TAB/LF/CR, other C0 controls, DEL U+007F, U+0080..U+009F,',
      'NBSP and other Zs, U+2028/U+2029, U+200B and other Cf, unassigned Cn',
      'like U+0378, private use, printable non-ASCII (accents, CJK), astral',
      'emoji, lone-ish astral pairs, and combinations. Verify the \\xHH /',
      '\\uHHHH / \\UHHHHHHHH forms and lower-case hex. Feed bytes via bash',
      "$'...' or printf so you control them exactly. Diff stderr excluding only",
      'the [PYI-<pid>] number.',
    ].join(' '),
  },
  {
    key: 'argparse-surfaces',
    prompt: [
      'Differential-test every CLI surface: no args, --help, -h, --a with and',
      'without a value, --a= forms (including --a= empty), repeated --a,',
      'unknown long/short options, extra positionals, "--" separators,',
      'abbreviations (--h, --he, --hel, --ab, --a), values that start with "-"',
      '(-3, -4, -3.5, -, -abc, "-3 -4", "-3,-4"), interleavings like',
      '`--a 1 --b`, `--b --a 1`, `--a 1 extra more`, `-h --a x`, `--a x -h`.',
      'Check stdout vs stderr routing and the exact exit code for each.',
      'Confirm the error-precedence ordering (expected-one-argument, then',
      'required, then unrecognized). Diff byte-exactly.',
    ].join(' '),
  },
  {
    key: 'bucketize-output',
    prompt: [
      'Differential-test the bucketize result and its rendering: key',
      'first-insertion ordering (all-even, all-odd, even-first, odd-first,',
      'alternating, long sequences), single element, duplicates, zeros and',
      'negative zero, mixed signs, and large item counts (e.g. 200 values).',
      'Verify the exact separator bytes ", " and ": ", the braces/brackets, the',
      'True/False spelling, the trailing newline, and that there is exactly one',
      'trailing newline. Use od -c or cmp for byte-level confirmation.',
      'Also read the bucketize implementation and confirm it is a faithful,',
      'generic, insertion-ordered single-pass grouping rather than special-cased',
      'to booleans.',
    ].join(' '),
  },
  {
    key: 'compliance',
    prompt: [
      'Audit the HARD REQUIREMENTS rather than behaviour. Verify: every file',
      'under ' + OUT + ' ends in .mjs; the entry is exactly ' + OUT + '/test5.mjs;',
      'there is no `require(`, no `module.exports`, no `exports.` anywhere;',
      'every `import` specifier is either a relative path ending in .mjs or a',
      '`node:`-prefixed builtin (grep every import and list them);',
      'no package.json / node_modules / lockfile; no bare-specifier imports;',
      'no reference to any third-party JS library by name; no python',
      'invocation and no child_process usage in the shipped code; the library',
      'is genuinely split into multiple modules under lib/ that each export',
      'their interface; test5.mjs is a thin entry point. Also confirm the code',
      'runs on a clean cwd (`cd / && node ' + OUT + '/test5.mjs --a 1,2`) and',
      'that no file is dead/unimported. Report each violation as a mismatch.',
    ].join(' '),
  },
]

const runnerContext = [
  'Reference oracle: ' + REF + ' (run it directly; NEVER run `python`).',
  'Node port entry: ' + OUT + '/test5.mjs (run as `node ' + OUT + '/test5.mjs ...`).',
  '',
  'The full verified spec the port was built against follows. Use it as the',
  'contract, but the BINARY is the ground truth -- if the spec and the binary',
  'disagree, the binary wins and that itself is a finding.',
  '',
  SPEC,
].join('\n')

// --- Phase 1: implement -----------------------------------------------------

phase('Implement')

await agent(
  [
    'You are porting a Python program to Node.js ESM. Write the complete',
    'implementation into ' + OUT + ' now.',
    '',
    SPEC,
    '',
    '# Your job',
    '',
    '1. Create the directory structure and write every .mjs file.',
    '2. Implement the full spec above, including the Unicode, repr, BigInt,',
    '   digit-limit, traceback and argparse details.',
    '3. Then SELF-VERIFY with a differential loop before you finish. Write a',
    '   throwaway harness OUTSIDE ' + OUT + ' (e.g. /tmp/difftest.sh) that, for',
    '   each case, captures reference stdout/stderr/exit and node',
    '   stdout/stderr/exit and diffs them (masking only the [PYI-<pid>]',
    '   number). Run at least 80 cases drawn from every section of the spec.',
    '   Iterate until every case matches. Do NOT leave the harness in ' + OUT + '.',
    '4. Code quality matters: clear module boundaries, doc comments explaining',
    '   the Python semantics being emulated (especially the surprising ones:',
    '   the White_Space vs isprintable split, the digit-limit counting rules,',
    '   the error precedence, the negative-number matcher, and the % 2 == 0',
    '   sign subtlety).',
    '',
    'Report, as your final message: the file tree you created, the count of',
    'differential cases you ran and how many passed, and any case where you',
    'could not achieve parity (be honest -- a known gap is far more useful',
    'than a false claim of success).',
  ].join('\n'),
  { label: 'implement', phase: 'Implement', effort: 'high' },
)

// --- Phases 2-3: differential test / fix, loop until dry --------------------

const MAX_ROUNDS = 4
let round = 0
let outstanding = []

while (round < MAX_ROUNDS) {
  const roundNo = round + 1
  const diffPhase = 'Differential'
  const results = await parallel(
    DIMENSIONS.map((d) => () =>
      agent(
        [
          'You are an adversarial differential tester. Round ' + roundNo + '.',
          'Dimension: ' + d.key,
          '',
          runnerContext,
          '',
          '# Your assignment',
          d.prompt,
          '',
          '# Rules',
          '* DO NOT EDIT ANY FILE under ' + OUT + '. You are a tester, not a fixer.',
          '  Other testers are running concurrently; edits would collide.',
          '  Scratch files must go in /tmp.',
          '* Be exhaustive and try hard to BREAK the port. Generate many cases',
          '  programmatically, not just a handful by hand.',
          '* Report ONLY divergences you actually reproduced, with the exact',
          '  command and the observed vs expected bytes. Do not speculate.',
          '* The [PYI-<pid>] number differing is EXPECTED and is not a finding.',
          '* If everything you tried matches, return an empty mismatches array',
          '  and say what you covered.',
        ].join('\n'),
        { label: 'diff:' + d.key, phase: diffPhase, schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA, effort: 'high' },
      ),
    ),
  )

  const found = results.filter(Boolean).flatMap((r) => r.mismatches || [])
  log('Round ' + roundNo + ': ' + found.length + ' candidate mismatches from ' + results.filter(Boolean).length + '/' + DIMENSIONS.length + ' testers')

  if (!found.length) {
    outstanding = []
    log('Round ' + roundNo + ' came back clean.')
    break
  }

  // Adversarially verify each candidate before spending a fix on it.
  const verdicts = await parallel(
    found.map((m, i) => () =>
      agent(
        [
          'Independently verify a reported divergence between the Python',
          'reference binary and the Node port. Try to REFUTE it.',
          '',
          'Reference: ' + REF,
          'Port: node ' + OUT + '/test5.mjs',
          '',
          'Claim: ' + m.title,
          'Repro: ' + m.repro,
          'Reported expected (reference): ' + m.expected,
          'Reported actual (node): ' + m.actual,
          '',
          'Run the repro yourself against both. Set real=true ONLY if a genuine',
          'divergence (or a genuine hard-requirement violation) reproduces right',
          'now. Set real=false if it does not reproduce, if the only difference',
          'is the [PYI-<pid>] number, or if the reporter misread the output.',
          'Do not edit any file.',
        ].join('\n'),
        { label: 'verify:' + i, phase: diffPhase, schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA },
      ).then((v) => ({ m, v })),
    ),
  )

  const confirmed = verdicts.filter(Boolean).filter((x) => x.v && x.v.real).map((x) => x.m)
  log('Round ' + roundNo + ': ' + confirmed.length + ' of ' + found.length + ' confirmed after adversarial verification')

  if (!confirmed.length) {
    outstanding = []
    log('No candidate survived verification; treating the port as clean.')
    break
  }

  outstanding = confirmed

  await agent(
    [
      'You are fixing the Node ESM port at ' + OUT + '. Round ' + roundNo + '.',
      '',
      runnerContext,
      '',
      '# Confirmed divergences to fix (each was independently reproduced)',
      '',
      JSON.stringify(confirmed, null, 2),
      '',
      '# Rules',
      '* You are the ONLY writer this round. Fix all of the above.',
      '* After each fix, re-run its repro against BOTH binaries and confirm parity.',
      '* Then run a broad regression sweep (at least 60 cases spanning the whole',
      '  spec) to make sure you did not break previously-passing behaviour.',
      '* Keep the hard requirements intact: .mjs only, ESM only, zero external',
      '  deps, no require/module.exports, hierarchical lib/ modules, entry at',
      '  ' + OUT + '/test5.mjs, no package.json, no stray test harness inside ' + OUT + '.',
      '* Scratch/harness files go in /tmp only.',
      '',
      'Report which divergences you fixed, how you verified each, and any you',
      'deliberately did not fix (with the reason).',
    ].join('\n'),
    { label: 'fix:r' + roundNo, phase: 'Fix', effort: 'high' },
  )

  round++
}

// --- Phase 4: final audit ---------------------------------------------------

phase('Audit')

const audits = await parallel([
  () =>
    agent(
      [
        'Final byte-parity sweep of the Node ESM port against the reference.',
        '',
        runnerContext,
        '',
        'Build a comprehensive fuzz + table harness in /tmp (do not write inside',
        OUT + '). Include: a randomised fuzzer generating several hundred --a',
        'values mixing ASCII digits, Unicode Nd digits from several blocks,',
        'signs, underscores, whitespace from the full White_Space set, junk',
        'characters, control characters, astral characters, commas in awkward',
        'positions, and very long digit strings around the 4300 boundary; plus a',
        'table of every documented case in the spec; plus the CLI surfaces.',
        'For each case compare stdout, stderr (masking only the [PYI-<pid>]',
        'number) and the exit code.',
        '',
        'Report the total case count, the pass count, and every failure with its',
        'exact repro. Do not edit any file. Be rigorous and do not overstate.',
      ].join('\n'),
      { label: 'audit:parity', phase: 'Audit', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA, effort: 'high' },
    ),
  () =>
    agent(
      [
        'Final hard-requirements compliance audit of ' + OUT + '.',
        '',
        SPEC,
        '',
        'Check every numbered hard requirement mechanically (grep/ls/node) and',
        'report any violation as a mismatch. Additionally verify: the code has no',
        'syntax errors under `node --check` for every .mjs file; there are no',
        'unused/dead modules; no file inside ' + OUT + ' is a test harness or',
        'scratch file; running from an unrelated cwd works; and the module',
        'hierarchy is genuine (multiple focused modules, each exporting its',
        'interface, imported with explicit .mjs suffixes). Do not edit files.',
      ].join('\n'),
      { label: 'audit:compliance', phase: 'Audit', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA, effort: 'high' },
    ),
  () =>
    agent(
      [
        'Completeness critic for this Python-to-Node migration.',
        '',
        runnerContext,
        '',
        'Read every file under ' + OUT + '. Your job is to find what the other',
        'reviewers MISSED -- a Python semantic not emulated, a code path never',
        'exercised, an input class nobody tried, a hard requirement only',
        'partially met, a comment that misdescribes the code, or a place where',
        'the implementation happens to pass the tested cases for the wrong',
        'reason (e.g. a hardcoded lookup that would fail on an untested input).',
        'Probe the reference binary to settle any question. Report concrete,',
        'reproduced gaps only. Do not edit files.',
      ].join('\n'),
      { label: 'audit:critic', phase: 'Audit', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA, effort: 'high' },
    ),
])

const auditFindings = audits.filter(Boolean).flatMap((r) => r.mismatches || [])
log('Audit: ' + auditFindings.length + ' findings')

if (auditFindings.length) {
  await agent(
    [
      'Final fix pass on the Node ESM port at ' + OUT + '.',
      '',
      runnerContext,
      '',
      '# Audit findings to resolve',
      JSON.stringify(auditFindings, null, 2),
      '',
      'Fix every finding that is genuine. For each, re-verify against the',
      'reference binary. Then run a final broad regression sweep (100+ cases)',
      'and confirm the hard requirements still hold (.mjs only, ESM only, zero',
      'external deps, no require/module.exports, entry at ' + OUT + '/test5.mjs,',
      'no scratch files inside ' + OUT + ').',
      '',
      'Report what you changed, what you verified, and anything you chose to',
      'leave alone and why.',
    ].join('\n'),
    { label: 'final-fix', phase: 'Audit', effort: 'high' },
  )
}

const summary = await agent(
  [
    'Produce the final report for this migration.',
    '',
    runnerContext,
    '',
    'Do all of the following:',
    '1. List the exact file tree under ' + OUT + ' with a one-line purpose for each file.',
    '2. Run a final confirmation sweep of at least 40 representative cases',
    '   (success cases, int errors, argparse errors, --help, huge values,',
    '   Unicode digits, repr escaping) comparing stdout, stderr and exit code',
    '   against the reference. State the pass/fail counts truthfully.',
    '3. Confirm the hard requirements with actual commands and paste the key',
    '   evidence (the import list, the .mjs file list, the require/exports grep).',
    '4. State any remaining known divergence, or say plainly that none remain.',
    '',
    'Return this as a compact structured report. Do not edit files.',
  ].join('\n'),
  { label: 'summary', phase: 'Audit', effort: 'high' },
)

return {
  outstandingAfterLoop: outstanding.length,
  rounds: round,
  auditFindings: auditFindings.length,
  summary,
}
